meta.title: The Highest Border Crossing on Earth Shuts Down for Winter
meta._convention: Duration omitted per beat -- filled from measured narration length. Verified via WebSearch before scripting: Khunjerab Pass is at 36.85N, 75.428E (36 51'N 75 25'42"E), elevation 4,693m/15,397ft, on the Karakoram Highway between Sost, Pakistan (~74.86E,36.55N) and Tashkurgan, China (~75.23E,37.78N); closed roughly Dec-Mar under a 1985 bilateral agreement. Both PK (586) and CN (156) confirmed present in country-codes.json and the world-atlas 110m dataset, so highlight is used for both throughout; the pass/highway itself is carried by markers + an animated route line.

beats.voText: At over 15,000 feet, this is the highest paved international border crossing anywhere on Earth, and for months each year, it's completely buried in snow.
It's called the Khunjerab Pass, connecting Pakistan and China through the Karakoram Mountains, at nearly 4,700 meters above sea level.
The altitude is so extreme that altitude sickness is a real risk just from standing at the checkpoint, before you've even crossed the border.
Under a 1985 agreement, the pass only stays open from April through November, the rest of the year, snow makes it physically impassable.
When it reopens each spring, it's briefly one of the most remote functioning borders anyone can actually drive across, before winter shuts it again.
A road so high the mountains themselves close it for half the year, and it still reopens, every single spring. Follow for more places on Earth that shouldn't exist, but do.
